title.en: Vladimir Putin to arrive in Beijing for state visit hot on heels of Trump
title.zh: 普京抵达北京进行国事访问，紧随特朗普之后

summary.en: Russian President Vladimir Putin is set to arrive in Beijing for a state visit, marking his 25th trip to China. On the eve of his visit, Putin stated that relations between the two countries have reached an "unprecedented level." This visit follows closely after Donald Trump's departure from China.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京即将抵达北京进行国事访问，这是他第25次访问中国。在访问前夕，普京表示两国关系已达到“前所未有的水平”。此次访问紧随唐纳德·特朗普离开中国之后。

body.en:
Vladimir Putin is due to arrive in Beijing on Tuesday for a state visit, four days after Donald Trump left China.

Putin’s visit to China – his 25th, according to Chinese state media – reflects Beijing’s growing confidence on the world stage as a centre of global diplomatic activity.

It also underscores the deep relationship between Putin and China’s leader, Xi Jinping . The two men have met more than 40 times, far outstripping Xi’s encounters with any western leaders.

“Hosting two of the most powerful leaders in the world in a matter of days shows China’s growing confidence in its place and standing in the world,” said William Yang, a senior analyst at the International Crisis Group.

He said Xi “likely wants to remind Trump that Beijing has other solid and robust relationships that it can count on, so Washington can’t easily isolate or harm Beijing if it tries to”.

Putin’s visit comes as he is entering what may be the most difficult period of his long rule. His strongman image at home is beginning to fray as Russia has made little progress on the battlefield in Ukraine this year. Russia’s growing economic troubles are steadily increasing its dependence on China, turning what the Kremlin frames as a partnership of equals into a far more lopsided relationship.

The Russian leader published a video address to China on the eve of the visit. He said China-Russia relations had reached “an unprecedented level”, pointing to the countries’ soaring bilateral trade, the fact that settlements were conducted nearly entirely in roubles and yuan rather than the US dollar, and mutual visa-free policies for Chinese and Russian travellers.

China’s foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday: “The friendship between China and Russia will be further deepened and will be more deeply rooted in people’s hearts” by the strategic guidance from Xi and Putin.

This year marks 30 years since Beijing and Moscow signed a strategic partnership agreement and 25 years since they singed the “treaty of good-neighbourliness and friendly cooperation”.

Putin’s remarks about non-dollar-denominated transactions highlight the extent to which the two countries have been trying to build up their resilience against western sanctions, which rely on the dominance of the US dollar to be effective.

China does not comply with western sanctions on Russia and since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has bought more than $367bn of Russian fossil fuels, according to data collected by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.

title.en: Son of Mango boss arrested over father's fatal fall from cliff
title.zh: 芒果老板儿子因父亲坠崖身亡被捕

summary.en: Isak, 71, died in December 2024 after falling from a ravine while walking in the Montserrat mountains near Barcelona.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The son of Mango founder Isak Andic has been arrested in connection with his father's death.

Jonathan Andic, 43, was detained by Catalan police on Tuesday as part of a renewed investigation into the death of the fashion tycoon, which was initially treated as an accident but was later reopened.

Isak, 71, died in December 2024 after falling from a ravine while walking in the Montserrat mountains near Barcelona with his son. There have been conflicting media reports about whether they were alone or if other family members were present.

A family spokesperson told Reuters that Jonathan was being questioned and that the family was confident of his innocence.

He joined Mango in 2005 and later oversaw the company's Mango Man line. He became vice-chairman of the board after his father's death.

Investigators in Catalonia initially closed the case in early 2025 after finding no evidence of criminal wrongdoing but reopened it later that year, claiming there were inconsistencies in Jonathan's testimony, the La Vanguardia newspaper reported.

Jonathan was taken from his home shortly after 11:00 local time (09:00 GMT) where he was questioned by police again. He was expected to be taken to a court to testify before a judge later on Tuesday, the paper added.

Born in Turkey, Isak founded Mango with the help of his brother, Nahman, in Barcelona in 1984 and the chain now operates almost 3,000 outlets in 120 countries.

At the time of his death, Forbes estimated the businessman's net worth to be $4.5bn (£3.6bn).

Mango CEO Toni Ruiz previously said Isak's death would "leave a huge void" and added: "All of us are, in some way, his legacy and the testimony of his achievements".

"It is up to us, and this is the best tribute we can make to Isak and which we will fulfil, to ensure that Mango continues to be the project that Isak aspired to and of which he would feel proud."
body.zh: Mango 创始人伊萨克·安迪奇 (Isak Andic) 的儿子因与其父亲的死亡有关而被捕。 43 岁的乔纳森·安迪奇 (Jonathan Andic) 周二被加泰罗尼亚警方拘留，这是对这位时尚大亨死亡事件重新调查的一部分，该死因最初被视为意外事故，但后来重新调查。 71 岁的伊萨克 (Isak) 于 2024 年 12 月与儿子在巴塞罗那附近的蒙特塞拉特山脉散步时从峡谷坠落身亡。关于他们是否独自一人或是否有其他家庭成员在场，媒体的报道相互矛盾。 一位家庭发言人告诉路透社，乔纳森正在接受讯问，家人相信他是清白的。 他于 2005 年加入 Mango，随后负责该公司的 Mango Man 系列。父亲去世后，他成为董事会副主席。 据《先锋报》报道，加泰罗尼亚调查人员最初于 2025 年初结案，因为没有发现任何刑事不当行为的证据，但在当年晚些时候重新审理此案，声称乔纳森的证词存在不一致之处。 当地时间 11:00（格林威治标准时间 09:00）后不久，乔纳森被从家中带走，并再次接受警方讯问。该报补充说，预计他将于周二晚些时候被带到法庭向法官作证。 Isak 出生于土耳其，1984 年在其兄弟 Nahman 的帮助下在巴塞罗那创立了 Mango，该连锁店目前在 120 个国家/地区拥有近 3,000 家门店。 在他去世时，《福布斯》估计这位商人的净资产为 45 亿美元（36 亿英镑）。 Mango 首席执行官托尼·鲁伊斯 (Toni Ruiz) 此前表示，伊萨克的去世将“留下巨大的空白”，并补充道：“在某种程度上，我们所有人都是他的遗产和他成就的见证”。 “这取决于我们，这是我们能够向 Isak 做出的最好的致敬，我们将履行这一承诺，以确保 Mango 继续成为 Isak 所渴望的项目，并让他感到自豪。”

title.en: Father-of-8 killed in San Diego mosque shooting hailed as a hero
title.zh: 圣地亚哥清真寺枪击案中丧生的8个孩子的父亲被誉为英雄

summary.en: Security guard Amin Abdullah, one of three killed in the attack, was described as "a shining light".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The bravery of a security guard who was shot dead along with two other worshippers at a San Diego mosque on Monday prevented the attack from being much worse, say police.

The guard was Amin Abdullah, a father of eight, a spokeswoman for the Council on American-Islamic Relations-San Diego (Cair-SD), Tazheen Nizam, told the BBC.

"It's fair to say his actions were heroic," San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl told a news conference. "Undoubtedly, he saved lives today."

Abdullah and two others - whom Cair-SD named as Mansour Kaziha and Nader Awad - were killed by two yet-to-be-identified teenage attackers who then took their own lives, say police.

People who knew Abdullah told US media he looked after the community. Others have taken to social media to describe him as "the nicest man you'll ever meet".

The mosque called him "a courageous man who put himself on the line of the safety of others, who even in his last moments did not stop protecting our community".

Nizam, the Cair spokeswoman, told the BBC: "Amin was loved by everybody, he stood there day after day, always smiling, welcoming everybody, welcoming the kids who came to the school.

A friend of the family told the Associated Press that Abdullah was well-known at the mosque and had worked there for more than a decade.

"He wanted to defend the innocent so he decided to become a security guard," Shaykh Uthman Ibn Farooq, told the news agency.

Sam Hamideh knew Abdullah through the mosque and told the BBC's US partner CBS that the security guard would be remembered for his kindness.

"It didn't matter who walked up... any random person could just walk up and, like, [Abdullah] would greet them, make sure they are OK," Hamideh said.

"Whether they were homeless off the street looking for something, whether it was a child or elderly."

The other two victims were worshippers at the mosque, said Cair-SD. Kaziha helped maintain its grounds and convenience store. Awad's wife teaches at the school that is part of the Islamic centre.

The deadly shooting unfolded close to noon on Monday after the mother of one of the two alleged attackers called police to report that her son had run away with a friend and might be suicidal.

Hours later, as police were searching for the two teenagers, authorities found three victims with gunshot wounds outside the Islamic Center of San Diego, including Abdullah.

Shortly afterwards, police found the two suspects - aged 17 and 18 - dead of self-inflicted wounds in a vehicle blocks away from the mosque.

The shooting is being investigated as a hate crime, Wahl said, noting that "hate rhetoric" was involved.

title.en: What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

summary.en: An outbreak of Ebola in DR Congo involves a rare strain and is in an area affected by conflict.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been declared a public health emergency of international concern, by the World Health Organization (WHO).

The latest outbreak is challenging because it involves a rare strain of Ebola for which there is no vaccine, and cases have been found in an area affected by conflict.

The WHO has told the BBC that the outbreak may be spreading faster than originally thought.

Ebola viruses normally infect animals, typically fruit bats, but outbreaks among humans can sometimes start when people eat or handle infected animals.

It takes two to 21 days for symptoms to appear. They come on suddenly and start like the flu, with fever, headache and tiredness.

As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.

The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

This outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which had not been seen for over a decade.

Bundibugyo has only caused two previous outbreaks, when it killed about a third of those infected.

Initial blood tests for Ebola in the affected areas were negative as they were designed to identify the more common species of the disease.

There is no approved vaccine for Bundibugyo, but experimental ones are in development. It is possible that a vaccine for another species of Ebola called Zaire may offer some protection.

A further complication is that the outbreak is taking place in a conflict zone, with a quarter of million people displaced from their homes and people moving across porous borders into neighbouring countries.

However, the WHO's declaration of a public health emergency of international concern does not mean we are in the early stages of a Covid-style pandemic. The risk Ebola poses outside east Africa is minimal.

The first known case was a nurse who developed symptoms on 24 April, which means the virus had been spreading undetected for weeks.

She died in Bunia, the capital of eastern DR Congo's Ituri province, according to Congolese health minister Samuel Roger Kamba.

The nurse's body was repatriated to Mongwalu, one of two gold-mining towns where the majority of cases have been reported.

Kamba said one of the reasons the virus spread so quickly was the number of people exposed to the body during the funeral ceremony.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention told the BBC World Service that funerals were a particular concern, as they also helped spread the disease during previous outbreaks.

Director Dr Jean Kaseya said public health information campaigns were "providing information on how to handle funerals" and the importance of basic hygiene...
body.zh: 世界卫生组织（WHO）已将刚果民主共和国爆发的埃博拉疫情列为国际关注的突发公共卫生事件。 最近的疫情具有挑战性，因为它涉及一种罕见的埃博拉病毒，目前还没有疫苗，而且在受冲突影响的地区发现了病例。 世界卫生组织告诉英国广播公司，疫情的传播速度可能比最初想象的要快。 埃博拉病毒通常感染动物，通常是果蝠，但人类中的疫情有时可能在人们食用或处理受感染的动物时开始。 症状需要 2 至 21 天才会出现。它们发病突然，开始时像流感一样，伴有发烧、头痛和疲倦。 随着疾病的进展，出现呕吐和腹泻，并可能导致器官衰竭。有些（但不是全部）患者会出现内出血和外出血。 病毒通过接触血液或呕吐物等受感染的体液从一个人传播到另一个人。 这次疫情是由罕见的本迪布焦埃博拉病毒引起的，这种埃博拉病毒已经十多年没有出现过。 本迪布焦此前只爆发过两次疫情，当时约有三分之一的感染者死亡。 受影响地区的埃博拉病毒初步血液检测呈阴性，因为这些检测的目的是识别该疾病更常见的种类。 Bundibugyo 尚未获得批准的疫苗，但实验疫苗正在开发中。针对另一种埃博拉病毒扎伊尔的疫苗可能会提供一些保护。 更加复杂的是，疫情爆发在冲突地区，25万人流离失所，人们跨越漏洞百出的边境进入邻国。 然而，世界卫生组织宣布国际关注的突发公共卫生事件并不意味着我们正处于新冠病毒大流行的早期阶段。埃博拉在东非以外地区造成的风险很小。 第一个已知病例是一名护士，她于 4 月 24 日出现症状，这意味着该病毒已经在未被发现的情况下传播了数周。 刚果卫生部长塞缪尔·罗杰·坎巴表示，她在刚果民主共和国东部伊图里省首府布尼亚去世。 护士的尸体被运回蒙瓦卢，这是报告大多数病例的两个金矿城镇之一。 坎巴说，病毒传播如此之快的原因之一是葬礼期间接触尸体的人数。 非洲疾病控制和预防中心告诉英国广播公司国际台，葬礼是一个特别值得关注的问题，因为在之前的疫情爆发期间，葬礼也助长了疾病的传播。 主任让·卡塞亚博士表示，公共卫生信息活动“提供了如何处理葬礼的信息”以及基本卫生的重要性……

summary.en: A World Health Organization doctor has warned that Ebola may be spreading more rapidly than initially estimated in central Africa, with experts concerned that the actual number of cases could be significantly higher than the hundreds currently suspected.

body.en:
People living close to the epicentre of an Ebola outbreak which has killed 131 people have told BBC News of their fear, as a World Health Organization (WHO) representative warned cases may be spreading faster than originally thought.

One man in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province, the epicentre of the outbreak, said infected people were dying "very fast", and added: "Ebola has tortured us."

Officials said more than 513 cases were suspected in DR Congo as of Tuesday, while one person has died in neighbouring Uganda.

The WHO's Dr Anne Ancia told the BBC that the more the agency investigates the outbreak, the clearer it becomes cases have spread to other areas.

Modelling by the London-based MRC Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis released on Monday suggested there had been "substantial" under-detection, and that it could not rule out there had already been more than 1,000 cases.

The study suggested that the current outbreak is "larger than currently ascertained" and that its "true magnitude remains uncertain".

A man who spoke to BBC News and identified himself as Bigboy said people are "really scared" and doing what they can to protect themselves.

He said locals are taking precautions such as washing hands with clean water, but added that he wished they could get access to other protective supplies such as face masks.

Another Ituri local, Alfred Giza, said people in the community are aware of the threat and waiting to receive face masks to protect themselves, but that he would not know what to do if a family member or friend contracted the disease.

The Red Cross warned that Ebola can escalate quickly if cases are not identified early, communities lack information and health systems are overwhelmed, adding that "we are seeing all those conditions" in the current outbreak.

On Tuesday, DR Congo President Félix Tshisekedi called for "calm" and urged Congolese citizens to remain vigilant, after holding a crisis meeting on Monday evening.

WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, who declared the outbreak an international emergency last week, said he was "deeply concerned about the scale and speed of the epidemic".

It is feared the outbreak may have been ongoing for several weeks before it was first detected on 24 April.

There is no vaccine for the strain of Ebola virus fuelling the latest rise in cases, but the WHO is evaluating whether other drugs may provide protection.

Speaking to BBC Newsday, Ancia said DR Congo's Ituri province was a "very unsecured area with lots of movement of population", making it difficult for the agency to investigate and help control the disease.

She continued: "The more we are investigating this outbreak, the more we realise that it has already disseminated at least a little bit across border...

title.en: Czechia: Uproar over Sudeten German gathering in Brno
title.zh: 捷克：布尔诺苏台德德国集会引起轩然大波

summary.en: The first gathering of Sudeten Germans in Czechia since World War II is set to go ahead this weekend despite a political backlash that has exposed tensions over one of Central Europe's most painful historical legacies.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The first gathering of Sudeten Germans in Czechia since World War II is set to go ahead this weekend despite a political backlash that has exposed tensions over one of Central Europe's most painful historical legacies.

The annual Sudetendeutscher Tag, a meeting of ethnic Germans expelled from Czechoslovakia after the Second World War and their descendants, will take place in the Czech city of Brno from May 22 to 25 as part of the Meeting Brno festival of reconciliation.

But the event has triggered protests and a parliamentary declaration warning against what some Czech lawmakers called "historical revisionism" and the "relativization of Nazi crimes."

"The Chamber of Deputies expresses its opposition to the holding of the 76th convention of the Sudetendeutsche Landsmannschaft [Sudeten German Association] on the territory of the Czech Republic , in view of the historical context and the fact that attitudes questioning the postwar settlement have long appeared within parts of this movement," read the declaration passed in the lower house of the Czech parliament on Friday.

The motion, which was symbolic and non-binding, passed by 73 votes to none, with four abstentions.

Center-right opposition parties boycotted the debate, accusing the governing coalition — which includes the far-right SPD party — of exploiting the issue for political gain.

Prime Minister Andrej Babis has apparently changed his stance on the event. He recently said that the gathering in Brno is "not a fortunate development" despite having previously referred to it in neutral terms as a civic initiative that the Czech government was not dealing with.

The event has also drawn protests in Brno itself. Around 500 people joined a demonstration in April organized by the SPD.

The SPD is firmly opposed to the gathering and accuses Sudeten German organizations of seeking to overturn the postwar Benes decrees that confiscated German property and stripped ethnic Germans of citizenship.

This accusation is rejected by Bernd Posselt, chairman of the Sudeten German Association, the main organization representing Sudeten German expellees. Posselt has stressed that the Sudeten German Association no longer seeks to challenge the postwar order and described the event as an effort at reconciliation.

In 2015, the association made some key changes to its charter , among other things removing references to reparations and the reclamation of land.

Posselt, a former MEP for Bavaria's conservative Christian Social Union, told DW that the organization wanted an honest discussion of the past. He has since criticized the parliamentary declaration and insisted the gathering would go ahead.

body.zh: 尽管政治上的强烈反对暴露了中欧最痛苦的历史遗产之一的紧张局势，但二战以来苏台德德国人在捷克的首次集会仍将在本周末举行。 一年一度的苏台德意志大会（Sudetendeutscher Tag）是二战后被驱逐出捷克斯洛伐克的德意志人及其后裔的一次聚会，将于 5 月 22 日至 25 日在捷克布尔诺市举行，作为布尔诺和解节的一部分。 但这一事件引发了抗议活动，议会发表声明警告一些捷克议员所谓的“历史修正主义”和“纳粹罪行的相对化”。 捷克议会下院周五通过的声明中写道：“考虑到历史背景以及该运动部分地区长期以来存在质疑战后解决方案的态度，众议院表示反对在捷克共和国境内举行苏台德德国协会第76届代表大会。” 该动议具有象征性，不具约束力，以 73 票对零票、四票弃权获得通过。 中右翼反对党抵制这场辩论，指责包括极右翼社会民主党在内的执政联盟利用这一问题谋取政治利益。 总理安德烈·巴比斯显然改变了对这一事件的立场。他最近表示，布尔诺的集会“并不是一个幸运的事态发展”，尽管他之前曾用中性的措辞将其称为捷克政府没有处理的公民倡议。 该事件还引起了布尔诺本身的抗议。大约 500 人参加了社民党 4 月份组织的示威活动。 社会民主党坚决反对这次集会，并指责苏台德德国组织试图推翻战后没收德国财产并剥夺德国人公民身份的贝奈斯法令。 代表苏台德德国被驱逐者的主要组织苏台德德国协会主席伯恩德·波塞尔特驳斥了这一指控。波塞尔特强调，苏台德德国协会不再寻求挑战战后秩序，并将此次活动描述为和解的努力。 2015年，该协会对其章程进行了一些重大修改，其中删除了有关赔偿和开垦土地的内容。 巴伐利亚保守基督教社会联盟前欧洲议会议员波塞尔特告诉德国之声，该组织希望对过去进行诚实的讨论。此后他批评了议会的声明，并坚称集会将继续进行。 布尔诺会议节的组织者还发表声明称，聚会将按以下方式进行：

body.en:
The Australian government is urgently seeking information on the whereabouts and condition of seven Australian activists allegedly detained by Israel after boats in a Gaza-bound aid flotilla were intercepted by the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) in international waters overnight.

The location and condition of the Australians remains unknown, and the flotilla's media delegate confirmed there had been no contact with the activists since the delegation was intercepted.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) said it was urgently seeking confirmation of the welfare of Australians it believed to be detained.

"We will continue to make clear our expectation that any detainees receive humane treatment in line with international norms," a DFAT spokesperson said on Tuesday.

Flotilla organisers identified the Australian activists as Anny Mokotow, Dr Bianca Webb-Pullman, Neve O'Connor, Violet Coco, Gemma O'Toole, Sam Woripa Watson, Zack Schofield, Helen O'Sullivan, Juliet Lamont, Isla Lamont and Surya McEwan.

The Israeli foreign ministry said on X, that activists from the "provocation flotilla" had been transferred to Israeli vessels and claimed that no aid had been found on their boats.

The missing Australians' parents and loved ones called for immediate government action at a conference at the State Library Victoria on Tuesday.

Julie Webb-Pullman, the mother of general practitioner Dr Bianca Webb-Pullman, said she hadn't heard from her daughter since 8.09pm on Monday, as the flotilla was intercepted.

"Serial kidnappers have done it again, abducted my daughter in international waters while she was delivering humanitarian aid," she told reporters.

"Yet our pathetic prime minister cannot even rustle up a condemnation, let alone demand accountability."

Susie O'Toole said she hadn't had any direct contact with her 23-year-old daughter, Gemma, and assumed the cohort was on a prison cargo ship bound for Ashdod prison in Israel.

"Most probably they've been left out in the sun like most people previously have been, held in stress positions, not given water, not given food," she said.

"We are terrified about Gemma's well-being, we demand the Australian government do everything they can to get her home safely."

Neve O'Connor's father said: "It was made clear to the Sumud participants that the IDF could not guarantee the safety of any of the prisoners on the prison ship, and that those that had been kidnapped the first time would get special treatment."

"Neve was one of those people, so we have grave concerns for Neve, and all the Global participants."

body.zh: 就在接待唐纳德·特朗普几天后，中国国家主席习近平将迎来俄罗斯领导人弗拉基米尔·普京。这些会议凸显了北京在破碎的地缘政治格局中日益重要的作用。 表面上看，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京本周访华并会见习近平是为了纪念 2001 年《中俄睦邻友好合作条约》签署 25 周年。 但此行的时机值得注意，就在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普对北京进行国事访问几天后，它突显了中国在日益分裂和大国竞争的地缘政治格局中的影响力地位。 会议议题预计将包括双边经贸问题以及国际和地区事务的讨论。 在莫斯科因入侵乌克兰而与西方隔绝之际，中国已成为俄罗斯迄今为止最大的贸易伙伴，供应其进口产品的三分之一以上，并购买俄罗斯出口产品的四分之一以上。 但据报道，这种伙伴关系还具有军事层面。路透社 2025 年 7 月的一项调查称，中国公司涉嫌利用空壳公司向俄罗斯军火制造商运送无人机发动机作为工业冷却设备，但北京否认了这一指控。 在普京与习近平峰会之前，德国墨卡托中国研究中心（MERICS）的宋楚瑜告诉德国之声，当前的地缘政治格局使北京处于有利地位。 美国和俄罗斯现在都需要中国，尽管方式相反：华盛顿寻求战略竞争对手，而莫斯科则需要一个地缘政治和能源利益重叠的合作伙伴。 宋楚瑜补充说，与此同时，北京不需要倾向于平衡美国或远离俄罗斯与西方之间的紧张关系。 特朗普受到习近平的热情接待，并乐观地离开北京。普京此行的部分目的可能是寻求保证，即中美关系的任何进展都不会以莫斯科为代价。 对于普京来说，当务之急是重申他与习近平的密切关系，并评估北京目前的想法。宋楚瑜提出，一个更具前瞻性的问题是，如果俄罗斯寻求结束乌克兰战争，谁可以充当可靠的调解人。 最近的信号——包括更加温和的胜利日阅兵和乌克兰对俄罗斯石油基础设施的持续袭击——表明莫斯科可能正在经历战争疲劳。普京甚至暗示冲突可能即将结束。 自2022年2月俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以来，普京与习近平频繁会面。对于北京来说，这种关系仍然是一个战略优先事项，...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.

title.en: San Diego mosque shooting to be investigated as hate crime
title.zh: 圣地亚哥清真寺枪击案将作为仇恨犯罪调查

summary.en: Teenage gunmen have shot dead three men at the Islamic Center of San Diego before killing themselves. The incident is being treated as a hate crime by investigators.
summary.zh: 圣地亚哥伊斯兰中心发生枪击案，青少年枪手射杀了三名男子后自杀身亡。调查人员正将此事件作为仇恨犯罪处理。

body.en:
Teenage gunmen have shot dead three men at the Islamic Center of San Diego before killing themselves. The incident is being treated as a hate crime by investigators.

Two gunmen aged 17 and 18 carried out a  shooting attack at a mosque in the southern Californian city of San Diego on Monday, killing three men and then themselves.

The shooting is being investigated as a hate crime, with the two suspects reported by police to have engaged in "generalized hate rhetoric."

Police said the shooting at the mosque was preceded by a call by the mother of one of the shooters to police in the morning saying that the boy had run away with her weapons and vehicle and that she feared he was suicidal.

As police were searching for the boy, additionally alarmed by information that he was dressed in camouflage and had a companion, reports arrived of a shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, some 15 kilometers (9 miles) from the city center. 

The shooters were then found dead with apparently self-inflicted gunwounds in a vehicle stopped in the middle of a road nearby, according to San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl.

Wahl said a security guard at the mosque was among the three people killed in the attack and that his response had helped prevent more deaths.

The Islamic center also houses a school, but its director, Imam Taha Hassane, said none of the students was harmed.  

"And at this moment all that I can say is, sending our prayers and standing in solidarity with all the families in our community here," he said.

Hassane said the center promoted interfaith relations and that a group of non-Muslims had been visiting it earlier on Monday to learn more about Islam.

Wahl told reporters that police were, for the moment, "actively investigating this as a hate crime," saying that there "was definitely hate rhetoric that was involved." 

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who is the first Muslim mayor of a major American city, said the attack was "an apparent act of anti-Muslim violence."

"Islamophobia endangers Muslim communities across this country," he posted on X, adding that New York police were boosting deployments to mosques "out of an abundance of caution."

 "Worshippers anywhere should not have to fear for their lives," he wrote on X.

"Hate has no place in California, and we will not tolerate acts of terror or intimidation against communities of faith," he said, adding, "To the San Diego Muslim community: California stands with you."
body.zh: 十几岁的枪手在圣地亚哥伊斯兰中心开枪打死三名男子，然后自杀。调查人员将这一事件视为仇恨犯罪。 周一，两名年龄分别为 17 岁和 18 岁的枪手对加利福尼亚州南部城市圣地亚哥的一座清真寺进行了枪击袭击，杀死了三名男子，然后自杀。 这起枪击事件正在作为仇恨犯罪进行调查，警方报告称，两名嫌疑人参与了“普遍的仇恨言论”。 警方表示，在清真寺发生枪击事件之前，其中一名枪手的母亲早上打电话给警方，称这名男孩带着武器和车辆逃跑了，她担心他有自杀倾向。 当警方搜寻这名男孩时，还对他穿着迷彩服并有同伴的消息感到震惊，有报告称距离市中心约 15 公里（9 英里）的圣地亚哥伊斯兰中心发生枪击事件。 据圣地亚哥警察局长斯科特·瓦尔称，枪手随后被发现死在一辆停在附近路中间的车辆中，显然是自伤。 瓦尔说，在袭击中丧生的三人中有一名清真寺的保安，他的反应有助于防止更多人死亡。 该伊斯兰中心还设有一所学校，但其校长伊玛目塔哈·哈桑表示，没有学生受到伤害。 他说：“此时此刻，我能说的就是祈祷，并与我们社区的所有家庭站在一起。” 哈桑说，该中心促进了宗教间关系，周一早些时候，一群非穆斯林参观了该中心，以了解更多关于伊斯兰教的信息。 瓦尔告诉记者，警方目前正在“积极调查这起仇恨犯罪”，并表示“其中肯定涉及仇恨言论”。 纽约市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼是美国主要城市的第一位穆斯林市长，他表示这次袭击是“明显的反穆斯林暴力行为”。 他在 X 上发帖称，“伊斯兰恐惧症危及全国各地的穆斯林社区”，并补充说，纽约警方“出于高度谨慎”，正在加大对清真寺的部署。 “任何地方的崇拜者都不应该担心自己的生命安全，”他在 X 上写道。 他说：“仇恨在加州没有立足之地，我们不会容忍针对信仰社区的恐怖或恐吓行为。”他补充道，“圣地亚哥穆斯林社区：加州与你们站在一起。”

reflection.en: The tragic violence at the San Diego mosque, ending in the gunmen's own deaths, is a stark reminder of the destructive path of hatred. Jesus' words warn that those who resort to violence often find it turns back on themselves, highlighting the profound cost of such actions. May we seek paths that break cycles of harm rather than perpetuate them.
reflection.zh: 圣地亚哥清真寺发生的悲剧性暴力事件，以枪手自杀告终，这严酷地提醒我们仇恨的毁灭性道路。耶稣的话语警告说，所有动刀的，必死在刀下，这突显了此类行为的沉重代价。愿我们寻求打破伤害循环而非延续它的道路。

verse.textEn: All who draw the sword will die by the sword.
verse.textZh: 凡动刀的，必死在刀下。

title.en: Three people killed in San Diego mosque shooting, two suspected gunmen found dead
title.zh: 圣地亚哥清真寺枪击案致三人死亡，两名嫌疑枪手被发现死亡

summary.en: Authorities are investigating a shooting at an Islamic center in San Diego that killed three people as a hate crime, with two suspected gunmen found dead. The FBI has been called in.
summary.zh: 圣地亚哥一处伊斯兰中心发生枪击案，造成三人死亡，两名嫌疑枪手被发现死亡。当局正将此案作为仇恨犯罪进行调查，联邦调查局已介入。

body.en:
A shooting at a mosque complex in California killed three people on Tuesday AEST, with two suspected teenage gunmen later found dead in a car from self-inflicted gunshot wounds, police said.

Police said emergency response teams found the victims outside the sprawling Islamic Center of San Diego, before later finding the alleged shooters, aged 18 and 17, also dead. Police originally gave the elder shooter's age as 19.

TV footage from a helicopter showed armed response teams gathered outside a building, with one unidentified person lying in a pool of blood.

Dozens of patrol cars were lined up around the Islamic Center, described on its website as the largest mosque in San Diego county, which lies in southern California.

After a short period of lockdown when authorities advised residents to stay inside, San Diego police announced that the threat at the centre had been "neutralised".

"We received a call of an active shooter at the Islamic centre. Within four minutes, officers arrived on scene and observed immediately three deceased victims out in front," San Diego police chief Scott Wahl told reporters.

"We immediately began to deploy with an active shooter response into the mosque and adjacent school," he said, adding that police had received calls about more gunfire nearby, where a landscaper at work had been shot at but not hit.

All of the children who were attending a day school that is part of the mosque complex were accounted for and safe after the shooting, Wahl said.

He said the FBI was called in to assist in the investigation of the incident, which the police chief said authorities were treating as a hate crime.

Wahl said the mother of one of the two suspects had called police about two hours before the shooting to report that her son, whom she described as suicidal, had run away from home taking three guns she owned and her vehicle.

According to the chief, the mother said her son was with a companion and the two were dressed in camouflage.

Police initiated efforts to track down the youths and were dispatching patrols to a nearby shopping mall and the son's high school as a precaution when calls came in reporting the mosque shooting.

Outside the Islamic centre, police found a vehicle in the middle of the street with the alleged shooters dead inside.

"The suspects at this point appear to have died from self-inflicted gunshot wounds. There were no officers involved in firing their weapons," Wahl said.

Police said that a security guard at the Islamic centre was among the three victims killed. The identity of the other two fatalities was not immediately clear.

Officials credited the slain security guard as likely having helped prevent further bloodshed.

body.zh: 警方称，澳大利亚东部标准时间周二，加利福尼亚州一座清真寺发生枪击事件，造成三人死亡，随后发现两名疑似青少年枪手因自伤枪伤死在一辆汽车中。 警方表示，应急响应小组在圣地亚哥庞大的伊斯兰中心外发现了受害者，随后发现分别为 19 岁和 17 岁的涉嫌枪击者也已死亡。 直升机的电视画面显示，武装反应小组聚集在一座建筑物外，一名身份不明的人躺在血泊中。 数十辆巡逻车在伊斯兰中心周围排队，该中心在其网站上被描述为位于南加州圣地亚哥县最大的清真寺。 在当局建议居民呆在室内的短暂封锁之后，圣地亚哥警方宣布该中心的威胁已“消除”。 圣地亚哥警察局长斯科特·瓦尔告诉记者：“我们接到伊斯兰中心一名枪手的电话。四分钟内，警察赶到现场，立即发现前面有三名遇难者。” 他说：“我们立即开始向清真寺和附近的学校部署积极的枪手应对措施。”他补充说，警方接到电话称附近发生更多枪击事件，一名正在工作的园艺师遭到枪击，但没有击中。 瓦尔说，枪击事件发生后，所有在清真寺建筑群内的走读学校上学的孩子都已找到并安全。 他说，联邦调查局被召来协助调查这起事件，警察局长表示，当局将这起事件视为仇恨犯罪。 在伊斯兰中心外，警方在街道中央发现一辆汽车，据称枪手死在车内。 瓦尔说：“目前嫌疑人似乎是死于自伤枪伤。没有警察参与开枪。” 警方称，遇难的三名受害者包括伊斯兰中心的一名保安。另外两名死者的身份尚不清楚。 清真寺伊玛目塔哈·哈桑表示，清真寺内所有工作人员、教师和儿童都很安全。 “我们以前从未经历过这样的悲剧。此时此刻我所能说的就是祈祷并与我们社区的所有家庭站在一起，”他说。 他告诉记者：“我已经得到了一些早期的最新消息，但我们将回去认真研究。” 州长加文·纽瑟姆新闻办公室表示，他已听取了有关此次明显袭击事件的简报。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: The tragic loss of life in a hate crime at a place of worship reminds us of the deep divisions that can exist in society. Scripture calls us to remember that the stranger among us should be treated with the same love and respect as our own people, fostering a community where all can feel safe and valued.
reflection.zh: 在一个礼拜场所发生的仇恨犯罪导致生命悲剧，这提醒我们社会中可能存在的深刻分歧。圣经呼吁我们记住，对待我们中间的陌生人，应像对待我们自己的人一样充满爱和尊重，从而建立一个让所有人都能感到安全和被重视的社区。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Cuba warns of 'bloodbath' amid Trump pressure: Is a US attack looming?
title.zh: 古巴警告“血腥屠杀”，特朗普加大对哈瓦那施压

summary.en: Relations between the United States and Cuba have deteriorated sharply in recent days, with Cuba issuing a stark warning of potential violence as the U.S. increases pressure on Havana.
summary.zh: 近日，美国与古巴两国关系急剧恶化，随着美国加大对哈瓦那的施压，古巴发出了可能发生暴力的严峻警告。

body.en:
Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel has warned that any United States military action against the island would trigger a "bloodbath" with consequences for regional peace and stability.

His comments on Tuesday came after Axios reported on Sunday, citing classified intelligence, that Cuba had acquired more than 300 military drones and discussed plans to use them to attack US military assets.

Cuba has rejected the allegations, accusing the US of fabricating a case to justify possible military intervention.

Relations between the two countries have deteriorated sharply in recent days following a US indictment of a former Cuban leader, as the latter endures increasing economic hardship .

Reports of drones in Cuba could serve as a pretext for US military action, Axios reported, and reflect the extent to which the Trump administration views Cuba as a growing threat due to advances in drone warfare and the presence of Iranian military advisers in the capital Havana.

A senior US official told Axios the developments had heightened concerns in Washington.

Cuba has faced mounting economic strain since the US cut off its energy supplies following the January arrest of Nicolás Maduro, the president of its ally Venezuela.

Fuel shortages have worsened in recent weeks, and electricity is reportedly available for only one or two hours a day in many areas.

Reuters news agency reported last week, citing a US Department of Justice source, that prosecutors planned to indict former Cuban leader Raúl Castro over Cuba's 1996 shooting down of two planes operated by a humanitarian group.

Foreign minister Bruno Rodriguez defended Cuba's position in a social media post, saying the country, "like every nation in the world", has the right to legitimate self-defence against external aggression under the United Nations Charter and international law.

An indictment of Castro, 94, the brother of late revolutionary leader Fidel Castro and a central figure in the 1959 Cuban Revolution, would mark a significant escalation in pressure on Cuba by the Trump administration.

John Hart, a US politics expert and a member of the emeritus faculty at the Australian National University, told SBS News the US blocking of energy imports into Cuba is a "humanitarian disaster" with "no logic or rationality".

Discerning US President Donald Trump's strategy regarding the island is difficult, as, unlike his previous efforts to control Greenland, Cuba offers very little in terms of natural resources or strategic value.

"It seems to me that a lot of his (Trump's) talk about Cuba right now is trying to generate some sort of distraction from domestic issues in the US," he said.

body.zh: 古巴总统米格尔·迪亚斯-卡内尔周二警告说，美国针对该岛的任何军事行动都将引发“大屠杀”，对地区和平与稳定造成后果。 在他发表上述言论之前，Axios 周日援引机密情报报道称，古巴已采购了 300 多架军用无人机，并讨论了使用它们攻击美国军事资产的计划。 古巴否认了这些指控，指责美国捏造案件，为可能的军事干预辩护。 最近几天，在美国起诉古巴前领导人后，两国关系急剧恶化，后者正面临着日益严重的经济困难。 据 Axios 报道，有关古巴无人机的报道可能成为美国采取军事行动的借口，并反映出特朗普政府将古巴视为日益严重的威胁，因为无人机战争的进展以及伊朗军事顾问在哈瓦那的存在。 一位美国高级官员告诉 Axios，事态发展加剧了华盛顿的担忧。 自从一月份其盟友委内瑞拉总统被捕后美国切断其能源供应以来，古巴面临着越来越大的经济压力。 最近几周，燃料短缺情况进一步恶化，据报道，许多地区每天只能提供一到两个小时的电力。 路透社上周援引美国司法部消息人士的话说，检察官计划就古巴 1996 年击落两架人道主义组织运营的飞机一事起诉古巴前领导人劳尔·卡斯特罗。 古巴外交部长布鲁诺·罗德里格斯在社交媒体上发帖捍卫古巴的立场，称古巴“像世界上每个国家一样”，有权根据《联合国宪章》和国际法对外部侵略进行合法自卫。 94 岁的卡斯特罗是已故革命领袖菲德尔·卡斯特罗的兄弟，也是 1959 年古巴革命的核心人物，对他的起诉将标志着特朗普政府对古巴的压力显着升级。 美国财政部周一宣布，美国对九名古巴官员实施制裁，其中包括通讯部长、几名军事领导人和古巴情报局。 这些制裁是特朗普政府加大对古巴政府压力的更广泛努力的一部分，其中包括限制从委内瑞拉和墨西哥向古巴运送石油。 美国政府称古巴共产党政府腐败无能，并公开推动政权更迭。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普威胁要对向古巴供应燃料的国家实施制裁，从而加大了对该岛的压力，这一政策导致了大面积停电，并进一步削弱了古巴的经济实力。

reflection.en: When international tensions escalate and threats of violence emerge, it is natural to feel apprehension about the future. In such moments, the ancient promise reminds us not to fear, for 雅伟 is with us, strengthening and helping us through uncertainty. This divine presence offers a steadfast anchor amidst the shifting tides of global affairs.
reflection.zh: 当国际局势紧张升级，暴力威胁浮现时，人们对未来感到忧虑是自然的。在这样的时刻，古老的应许提醒我们不要惧怕，因为雅伟与我们同在，在不确定中加添我们的力量并帮助我们。这份神圣的同在，在全球事务变幻莫测的浪潮中，提供了一个坚定的锚。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: Trump says he held off new attack on Iran after Gulf countries' request
title.zh: 特朗普称应海湾国家要求暂缓对伊朗发动新袭击

summary.en: Trump stated that the US military remains ready for a "full, large scale assault" on Iran if a deal is not reached, but he had previously held off an attack following requests from Gulf countries.
summary.zh: 特朗普表示，如果未能达成协议，美国军方仍“准备好对伊朗发动全面、大规模的袭击”，但他此前已应海湾国家的要求暂缓了袭击。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday AEST he had held off on imminent plans to resume attacking Iran, as Tehran rebuffs his demands for ending the war.

Trump said that he stopped the purported attack plan at the behest of Gulf Arab allies, which Iran has threatened with reciprocal attacks if the United States and Israel relaunch their assault and end a nearly six-week ceasefire.

Trump, who had indefinitely extended the truce and made clear he wants to exit a war that has proven to be a political liability, said publicly that he had prepared a new attack for Tuesday.

The leaders of Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates asked him "to hold off on our planned Military attack of the Islamic Republic of Iran, which was scheduled for tomorrow, in that serious negotiations are now taking place," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

He said the Gulf allies voiced confidence in reaching an agreement "which will be very acceptable" to the United States and Middle Eastern nations and result in "NO NUCLEAR WEAPONS FOR IRAN!"

But Trump said he had instructed the US military to be "prepared to go forward with a full, large scale assault of Iran, on a moment's notice, in the event that an acceptable Deal is not reached."

Iran has repeatedly rebuffed Trump's offers on a deal and has exerted control over the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway into the Gulf, sending global oil prices spiralling.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei confirmed exchanges with the United States through mediator Pakistan and said Iran made clear its "concerns."

The country, whose supreme leader was killed in the initial US-Israeli strikes on 28 February but has proven resilient, is demanding the release of Iranian assets frozen abroad and the lifting of long-standing sanctions.

Baqaei said Iran was also demanding reparations for the "illegal and baseless" war and was "fully prepared for any eventuality" if the United States resumes military action.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, considered a moderate in a system increasingly dominated since the war by the Revolutionary Guards, said that speaking with Washington in search of a deal was not to be viewed negatively.

"Dialogue does not mean surrender. The Islamic Republic of Iran enters into dialogue with dignity, authority, and the preservation of the nation's rights, and will under no circumstances retreat from the legal rights of the people and the country," he wrote on X.

On Sunday, Iran's Fars news agency said the US had presented a five-point list, which included a demand for Iran to keep only one nuclear site in operation and transfer its stockpile of highly enriched uranium to the United States.

title.en: Vladimir Putin to arrive in Beijing for state visit hot on heels of Trump
title.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京紧随特朗普抵达北京进行国事访问

summary.en: Russian leader says relations between two countries have reached ‘unprecedented level’ on eve of 25th visit to China Vladimir Putin is due to arrive in Beijing on Tuesday for a state visit, four days after Donald Trump left China. Putin’s visit to China – his 25th, according to...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Vladimir Putin is due to arrive in Beijing on Tuesday for a state visit, four days after Donald Trump left China.

Putin’s visit to China – his 25th, according to Chinese state media – reflects Beijing’s growing confidence on the world stage as a centre of global diplomatic activity.

It also underscores the deep relationship between Putin and China’s leader, Xi Jinping . The two men have met more than 40 times, far outstripping Xi’s encounters with any western leaders.

“Hosting two of the most powerful leaders in the world in a matter of days shows China’s growing confidence in its place and standing in the world,” said William Yang, a senior analyst at the International Crisis Group.

He said Xi “likely wants to remind Trump that Beijing has other solid and robust relationships that it can count on, so Washington can’t easily isolate or harm Beijing if it tries to”.

Putin’s visit comes as he is entering what may be the most difficult period of his long rule. His strongman image at home is beginning to fray as Russia has made little progress on the battlefield in Ukraine this year. Russia’s growing economic troubles are steadily increasing its dependence on China, turning what the Kremlin frames as a partnership of equals into a far more lopsided relationship.

The Russian leader published a video address to China on the eve of the visit. He said China-Russia relations had reached “an unprecedented level”, pointing to the countries’ soaring bilateral trade, the fact that settlements were conducted nearly entirely in roubles and yuan rather than the US dollar, and mutual visa-free policies for Chinese and Russian travellers.

China’s foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday: “The friendship between China and Russia will be further deepened and will be more deeply rooted in people’s hearts” by the strategic guidance from Xi and Putin.

This year marks 30 years since Beijing and Moscow signed a strategic partnership agreement and 25 years since they singed the “treaty of good-neighbourliness and friendly cooperation”.

Putin’s remarks about non-dollar-denominated transactions highlight the extent to which the two countries have been trying to build up their resilience against western sanctions, which rely on the dominance of the US dollar to be effective.

China does not comply with western sanctions on Russia and since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has bought more than $367bn of Russian fossil fuels, according to data collected by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.

title.en: China's moment? Putin heads to Beijing after Trump courts Xi
title.zh: 中国时刻？特朗普会晤习近平后，普京将前往北京

summary.en: China's President Xi Jinping is preparing to host Russian leader Vladimir Putin, following a recent meeting with Donald Trump. These high-profile diplomatic engagements underscore China's increasing influence in a complex and divided global political environment.
summary.zh: 在中国国家主席习近平会见唐纳德·特朗普后不久，他将迎来俄罗斯领导人弗拉基米尔·普京。这些高层外交活动凸显了中国在一个复杂且分裂的全球政治格局中日益增长的作用。

body.zh: 就在接待唐纳德·特朗普几天后，中国国家主席习近平将迎来俄罗斯领导人弗拉基米尔·普京。这些会议凸显了北京在破碎的地缘政治格局中日益重要的作用。 表面上看，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京本周访华并会见习近平是为了纪念 2001 年《中俄睦邻友好合作条约》签署 25 周年。 但此行的时机值得注意，就在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普对北京进行国事访问几天后，它突显了中国在日益分裂和大国竞争的地缘政治格局中的影响力地位。 会议议题预计将包括双边经贸问题以及国际和地区事务的讨论。 在莫斯科因入侵乌克兰而与西方隔绝之际，中国已成为俄罗斯迄今为止最大的贸易伙伴，供应其进口产品的三分之一以上，并购买俄罗斯出口产品的四分之一以上。 但据报道，这种伙伴关系还具有军事层面。路透社 2025 年 7 月的一项调查称，中国公司涉嫌利用空壳公司向俄罗斯军火制造商运送无人机发动机作为工业冷却设备，但北京否认了这一指控。 在普京与习近平峰会之前，德国墨卡托中国研究中心（MERICS）的宋楚瑜告诉德国之声，当前的地缘政治格局使北京处于有利地位。 美国和俄罗斯现在都需要中国，尽管方式相反：华盛顿寻求战略竞争对手，而莫斯科则需要一个地缘政治和能源利益重叠的合作伙伴。 宋楚瑜补充说，与此同时，北京不需要倾向于平衡美国或远离俄罗斯与西方之间的紧张关系。 特朗普受到习近平的热情接待，并乐观地离开北京。普京此行的部分目的可能是寻求保证，即中美关系的任何进展都不会以莫斯科为代价。 对于普京来说，当务之急是重申他与习近平的密切关系，并评估北京目前的想法。宋楚瑜提出，一个更具前瞻性的问题是，如果俄罗斯寻求结束乌克兰战争，谁可以充当可靠的调解人。 最近的信号——包括更加温和的胜利日阅兵和乌克兰对俄罗斯石油基础设施的持续袭击——表明莫斯科可能正在经历战争疲劳。普京甚至暗示冲突可能即将结束。 自2022年2月俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以来，普京与习近平频繁会面。对于北京来说，这种关系仍然是一个战略优先事项，...

summary.en: European trade analysts are warning of a potential "China shock" as the continent's industries become increasingly reliant on imported components from China. title.en: How China became Russia's economic lifeline
title.zh: 中国如何成为俄罗斯的经济生命线

summary.en: Following Donald Trump's visit, Russian President Vladimir Putin traveled to Beijing for discussions with Xi Jinping. The report examines how China's trade and financial assistance are crucial in sustaining Russia's economy.
summary.zh: 在唐纳德·特朗普访问之后，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京前往北京与习近平举行会谈。德国之声的报道探讨了中国的贸易和金融支持如何帮助俄罗斯经济维持运转。

body.en:
Hot on the heels of Donald Trump's visit, Russian President Vladimir Putin travels to Beijing for talks with Xi Jinping. DW explores how China's trade and financial support is helping keep Russia's economy afloat.

Russia may celebrate its "no-limits" partnership with China — a phrase coined when President Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping met just before the Ukraine war — yet those relations are increasingly one-sided.

Although bilateral trade softened last year as a result of lower oil prices, Russia’s goods exports to China have nearly doubled since February 2022, when Moscow's full-scale invasion began. 

In 2024, Russia shipped roughly $129 billion (€111 billion) worth of goods to China — the overwhelming majority in crude oil, coal and natural gas sold at steep discounts.

The Center for Research on Energy and Clean Air calculated that China has bought more than €319 billion ($372 billion) of Russian fossil fuels since the conflict began, giving Moscow vital hard currency to fund its military amid Western sanctions.

In return, China exported nearly $116 billion worth of goods to Russia in 2024, supplying machinery, electronics and vehicles that replaced Western suppliers who exited the Russian market.

Although Beijing has stopped short of direct exports to Russia of finished military hardware, China has supplied billions of dollars' worth of dual-use goods — civilian products and technologies that also have military applications. These have also helped sustain Russia’s defense industry.

As Putin and Xi prepare to meet in Beijing this week for high-level talks — timed to mark the 25th anniversary of the two countries' cooperation treaty — this growing imbalance leaves Moscow increasingly vulnerable to Beijing’s priorities.

Western sanctions , imposed since 2022 and repeatedly tightened, have severed Russia’s access to advanced Western technology.

The United States , European Union , United Kingdom and allies banned exports of semiconductors, microelectronics, precision machine tools and other dual-use goods critical for weapons production. These moves created acute shortages in Russia.

In response, Moscow turned to China, which, according to Bloomberg, supplied roughly 90% of Russia’s sanctioned technology imports in 2025 — up from 80% the previous year.

Obtaining goods like machine tools for missile and drone assembly is far more difficult and expensive than before the war. Russia must utilize complex evasion networks through third countries and often ends up paying premiums of nearly 90% above pre-war prices.

body.zh: 继唐纳德·特朗普访问之后，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京前往北京与习近平举行会谈。德国之声探讨了中国的贸易和金融支持如何帮助保持俄罗斯经济的发展。 俄罗斯可能会庆祝其与中国的“无限制”伙伴关系——这是弗拉基米尔·普京总统和习近平在乌克兰战争前夕会面时创造的一个短语——但这些关系却日益一边倒。 尽管去年双边贸易因油价下跌而疲软，但自2022年2月莫斯科开始全面入侵以来，俄罗斯对中国的商品出口几乎翻了一番。 2024 年，俄罗斯向中国出口了价值约 1,290 亿美元（1,110 亿欧元）的商品，其中绝大多数是以大幅折扣出售的原油、煤炭和天然气。 能源和清洁空气研究中心计算出，自冲突爆发以来，中国已购买了超过 3190 亿欧元（3720 亿美元）的俄罗斯化石燃料，这为莫斯科在西方制裁期间提供了重要的硬通货来为其军事提供资金。 作为回报，中国在 2024 年向俄罗斯出口了价值近 1160 亿美元的商品，提供机械、电子产品和车辆，取代了退出俄罗斯市场的西方供应商。 尽管北京方面已停止向俄罗斯直接出口成品军事硬件，但中国已提供了价值数十亿美元的军民两用商品——民用产品和技术，也可用于军事用途。这些也有助于维持俄罗斯的国防工业。 随着普京和习近平准备本周在北京举行高层会谈——纪念两国合作条约签署 25 周年——这种日益严重的不平衡使莫斯科越来越容易受到北京优先事项的影响。 西方制裁自2022年起实施并一再收紧，切断了俄罗斯获得西方先进技术的途径。 美国、欧盟、英国和盟国禁止出口半导体、微电子、精密机床和其他对武器生产至关重要的军民两用商品。这些举措造成了俄罗斯的严重短缺。 作为回应，莫斯科转向中国，据彭博社报道，到 2025 年，中国将提供俄罗斯受制裁技术进口的约 90%，高于前一年的 80%。 获得用于导弹和无人机组装的机床等商品比战前更加困难和昂贵。俄罗斯必须通过第三国利用复杂的逃税网络，最终往往要支付比战前价格高出近 90% 的保费。 北京还向俄罗斯提供了地球观测情报、用于军事目的的卫星图像和无人机……

title.en: Trump told Taiwan not to 'go independent' - but does it want to?
title.zh: 特朗普告诉台湾不要“独立”——但它想独立吗？

summary.en: Taiwan independence is the reddest of red lines for China, which claims the island as its own.
summary.zh: 台湾独立是中国最敏感的红线，中国声称该岛是其领土。

body.en:
Hours after meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing last week, Donald Trump issued a stern warning to Taiwan against pursuing independence.

"I'm not looking to have somebody go independent. And, you know, we're supposed to travel 9,500 miles to fight a war. I'm not looking for that. I want them to cool down. I want China to cool down," he told Fox News in an interview that aired on Friday.

Trump's comments - some of the strongest a US president has made so far on the issue - immediately sparked a flurry of responses from Taiwan saying it does not see the need to formally declare independence.

Taiwanese independence is the reddest of red lines for Beijing, which claims Taiwan as its own and has accused its president Lai Ching-te of being a separatist.

It dates back to the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949, when the Chinese Communist Party won control of China and the losing Kuomintang forces retreated to Taiwan, relocating its government to Taipei.

Beijing has since claimed the self-governed island. But after Xi came to power, the Chinese government has doubled down on its threats and sought ways to stamp out what it sees as separatism. Taiwan's "reunification" with China has become a key goal - Xi himself has called it an "unstoppable" reality.

In recent years, China has stepped up various forms of pressure, through military drills that have simulated blockades; the diplomatic isolation of Taiwan; and greyzone warfare where it sends warships and fighter jets close to Taiwanese waters and airspace on a regular basis.

During last week's summit, Xi had told Trump that the issue of Taiwan was the most important one in US-China relations, and that mishandling it could lead to conflict.

As the US is Taiwan's closest ally - it is bound by law to provide the island with the means to defend itself - observers have long worried that any attack on Taiwan would draw the US into direct conflict with China.

China has made clear its stance on Taiwan in its Anti-Secession Law, introduced in 2005, in which it states that it wants "peaceful reunification" with the island.

But the Anti-Secession Law also states that should "Taiwan independence" forces cause secession from China, or the possibility of "peaceful reunification" has been exhausted, China can employ "non-peaceful means" to protect its territorial integrity.

What this means is that China does not rule out the use of military force to take Taiwan if it deems it necessary. Most people believe that a formal declaration of independence by Taiwan's government would trigger this response.

body.zh: 上周在北京会见中国国家主席习近平几小时后，唐纳德·特朗普向台湾发出严厉警告，不要追求独立。 “我不希望有人独立。而且，你知道，我们应该行驶 9,500 英里去打一场战争。我不是在寻找那样的结果。我希望他们冷静下来。我希望中国冷静下来，”他在周五播出的福克斯新闻采访中说道。 特朗普的言论是迄今为止美国总统在这个问题上发表的最强烈的言论之一，立即引发了台湾的一系列反应，称台湾认为没有必要正式宣布独立。 台独是北京最红的红线，北京宣称台湾是自己的，并指责台湾总统赖清德是分裂分子。 这可以追溯到1949年中国内战结束时，当时中国共产党控制了中国，失败的国民党军队撤退到台湾，政府迁往台北。 此后，北京宣称对该岛拥有主权。但习近平上台后，中国政府加大了威胁力度，并寻求消除其眼中的分裂主义的方法。台湾与中国的“统一”已成为一个关键目标——习近平本人称其为“不可阻挡”的现实。 近年来，中国通过军事演习、模拟封锁等方式加大了各种形式的压力；对台湾的外交孤立；以及灰色地带战，定期派遣军舰和战斗机接近台湾海域和空域。 在上周的峰会上，习近平告诉特朗普，台湾问题是美中关系中最重要的问题，处理不当可能会导致冲突。 由于美国是台湾最亲密的盟友——它有法律义务向台湾提供自卫手段——观察人士长期以来一直担心对台湾的任何攻击都会使美国陷入与中国的直接冲突。 中国在2005年出台的《反分裂国家法》中明确表明了其对台湾的立场，其中表示希望与台湾“和平统一”。 但《反分裂国家法》也规定，如果“台独”势力从中国分裂出去，或者“和平统一”的可能性已经耗尽，中国可以采取“非和平方式”维护领土完整。 这意味着，如果中国认为有必要，不排除使用武力收复台湾。大多数人认为，台湾政府正式宣布独立就会引发这种反应。 台湾与中国有着密切的经济和文化联系。但拥有健全民主制度的台湾，大多数人认为自己在政治上与中国截然不同，而中国已变得越来越……

title.en: What really holds China and Russia together
title.zh: 是什么真正将中国和俄罗斯联系在一起

summary.en: The relationship endures despite a power imbalance, with both sides recognising that it is too important to fail.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As they strolled through Tiananmen Square in Beijing last September, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared to muse over the possibility that organ transplants could dramatically extend human life.

"Human organs can be continuously transplanted. The longer you live, the younger you become, and even achieve immortality", Putin's interpreter was heard saying.

"Some predict that in this century, humans may live up to 150 years old," Xi's interpreter was heard responding.

It was a fitting conversation for two strongmen, who have described each other as best friends, and who, after a combined 39 years in power, show no signs of stepping down.

This was a rare insight into what is quite a misunderstood partnership. This scrap of unscripted conversation is one of the few glimpses into a highly secretive relationship.

Putin will be returning to Beijing this week, coinciding with the 25th anniversary of the Treaty of Good-Neighbourliness and Friendly Cooperation between Russia and China.

When US President Donald Trump visited Xi last week he was met with an extravaganza of banquets with gold tableware and a visit to an ancient temple. Putin's visit feels far more low-key, with little information released in advance.

The Kremlin's spokesperson said they hoped to hear first-hand information about the Trump-Xi meeting.

Xi reportedly name-dropped his friend Putin to Trump last week, when the two leaders walked through Zhongnanhai, which is normally off-limits to foreign visitors, joking about how Putin had visited Beijing's political sanctuary before.

While some in Washington may have been hoping that Trump could wean Beijing off Moscow, such hopes appear little more than wishful thinking.

China and Russia have in recent years described their ties as a "friendship with no limits". So, what is this based on, and will their love affair last?

The relationship is highly uneven, and any deals struck between the two countries will likely be on Chinese terms, says Alexander Gabuev, director of the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center think tank. He stresses, "Russia is fully in China's pocket, and China can dictate the terms."

This dynamic persists across many sectors, not least the economy. China is Russia's largest trading partner, while Russia makes up just 4% of China's international trade. China exports more than any other country to Russia, and its economy is significantly larger than Russia's.

Years of western sanctions have gradually pushed Moscow deeper into trade engagement with Beijing. body.zh: 去年九月，当中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京漫步在北京天安门广场时，他们似乎在思考器官移植可以大幅延长人类寿命的可能性。 普京的翻译说：“人体器官可以不断移植。你活得越久，你就越年轻，甚至可以达到永生”。 “有人预测，本世纪，人类可能活到150岁，”习近平的翻译回答道。 对于两位强人来说，这是一次恰如其分的对话，他们称对方为最好的朋友，并且在执政 39 年后，没有表现出下台的迹象。 这是对一种被严重误解的伙伴关系的罕见洞察。这段即兴对话是为数不多的一段高度秘密关系的一瞥。 普京将于本周返回北京，恰逢俄中睦邻友好合作条约签署25周年。 当美国总统唐纳德·特朗普上周访问习近平时，他受到了盛大的宴会和金餐具的欢迎，并参观了一座古老的寺庙。普京的访问感觉要低调得多，事先几乎没有发布任何信息。 克里姆林宫发言人表示，希望听到有关特习会的第一手信息。 据报道，上周，当两位领导人走过通常禁止外国游客进入的中南海时，习近平向特朗普点名了他的朋友普京，并开玩笑说普京以前曾访问过北京的政治庇护所。 尽管华盛顿的一些人可能希望特朗普能够让北京摆脱莫斯科的影响，但这种希望似乎只不过是一厢情愿。 近年来，中国和俄罗斯将两国关系描述为“无限的友谊”。那么，这是基于什么，他们的恋情会持续下去吗？ 卡内基俄罗斯欧亚中心智库主任亚历山大·加布耶夫表示，两国关系极不平衡，两国之间达成的任何协议都可能按照中国的条件进行。他强调，“俄罗斯完全在中国的口袋里，中国可以决定条款。” 这种动态在许多领域持续存在，尤其是经济领域。中国是俄罗斯最大的贸易伙伴，而俄罗斯仅占中国国际贸易的4%。中国对俄罗斯的出口超过任何其他国家，其经济规模也明显大于俄罗斯。 多年的西方制裁逐渐促使莫斯科加深与北京的贸易接触。科技巨头华为受到美国制裁，并在英国政府审查后被迫退出英国 5G 网络，该公司利用西方公司的缺乏，成为俄罗斯的关键支柱。

title.en: Australia orders firms to sell stakes in rare earths miner
title.zh: 澳大利亚命令公司出售稀土矿商股份

summary.en: Australia's treasurer ordered China-linked companies to divest their stakes in Northern Minerals, a rare earths miner, citing the need to protect Australia's national interests.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚财政部长命令与中国有关联的公司剥离其在稀土矿商北方矿业的股份，理由是需要保护澳大利亚的国家利益。

body.zh: 财政部长命令与中国有联系的公司剥离北方矿业公司以保护澳大利亚的利益。 澳大利亚命令与中国有关的股东出售其在正在开发稀土矿的北方矿业公司的股份。 财务主管吉姆·查尔默斯 (Jim Chalmers) 表示，由于担心中国投资者试图控制北方矿产公司，他已于周一发布了命令。 这家总部位于澳大利亚的矿业公司正在西澳大利亚州最北部开发布朗斯山脉项目，以开采大量的镝和铽储量。 查尔默在一份声明中表示，他的决定旨在保护该国的国家利益并确保遵守其外国投资框架。 他说：“我们运营着一个强大且非歧视性的外国投资框架，如果需要，我们将采取进一步行动，以保护我们与此事相关的国家利益。” 镝和铽是对于耐热高性能磁体至关重要的重稀土元素。这些产品用于清洁能源应用，例如混合动力汽车和风力涡轮机，以及专业国防应用。 它开采约 60% 的原材料，并精炼约占全球供应量的 95%-98%。这使其几乎垄断了加工商业镝。 北方矿业公司的稀土预计将在澳大利亚新建的炼油厂进行加工。 当这两个项目上线时，澳大利亚将成为第一个重要的非中国加工镝来源国。 包括澳大利亚和美国在内的西方国家正在寻求限制中国对关键矿产的投资。 近年来，中国投资者一直寻求在北方矿业公司持有大量股份。 关于查尔默最近的处置令，六名股东中有三名的地址在中国，两名在香港，一名在英属维尔京群岛上市。 但早在 2024 年，澳大利亚就已经利用外国收购法迫使五名投资者出售其在北方矿业公司的股份。 2025 年，财政部采取了史无前例的举措，将最大股东之一告上法庭，称其藐视出售令，而是将股份转入其自己董事的名下。

reflection.en: Nations, like individuals, often face complex decisions to safeguard their future and resources. This action by Australia's treasurer reflects a strategic move to protect perceived national interests in a critical industry. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing potential challenges and taking prudent steps to secure what is vital.

title.en: EV battery supply chains in focus as China halts sulphuric acid exports
title.zh: 中国暂停硫酸出口，电动汽车电池供应链受关注

summary.en: China's decision to stop exporting sulphuric acid is expected to create pressure on global supply chains for both electric vehicle batteries and fertilizers.
summary.zh: 中国停止出口硫酸预计将对电动汽车电池和化肥的全球供应链造成压力。

body.en:
China has banned exports of sulphuric acid, the world's most used industrial chemical and a crucial ingredient in battery and clothing manufacturing, as well as fertiliser production and metal processing industries.

The move comes amid pressures on supply of the chemical after conflict in the Middle East disrupted sulphur shipments through the Strait of Hormuz earlier this year.

Marina Zhang from the University of Technology Sydney's Australia-China Relations Institute said that, while the ban may have been presented by China as temporary, it signals a policy shift from Australia's largest trading partner towards increasingly prioritising control over industrial inputs.

"It's not just finished products, but the upstream materials, processing technologies and basic industrial ingredients that allow advanced manufacturing to scale … So while the immediate measure may be temporary, the underlying logic is structural," Zhang told SBS News.

Sulphur is the primary ingredient used to produce sulphuric acid, meaning shipping and processing delays of the raw material in the Gulf region have created flow-on effects for manufacturers reliant on a steady supply.

In 2025, about half of the global seaborne supply of sulphur came from the Middle East.

China accounted for a significant share of sulphuric acid shipments from Asia last year and remains one of the world's largest exporters. The loss of that supply is now raising concerns among overseas buyers already scrambling to secure alternative sources.

While the impacts are expected to be spread across multiple industries, analysts say battery supply chains could be among the most exposed.

Zhang said the situation "reveals a paradox at the heart of the clean-energy transition … which depends on minerals that require very energy-intensive, chemical-intensive and often environmentally difficult processing".

"Yet many Western countries have spent decades outsourcing precisely those 'dirty' industrial activities."

Sulphuric acid also plays an important role in processing metals such as nickel and copper, both used extensively in electric vehicle batteries and energy storage systems.

Indonesia's rapidly expanding nickel-processing industry is considered particularly vulnerable to the bans.

The country has become a major producer of battery-grade nickel used in global electric vehicle (EV) supply chains, including by manufacturers linked to Chinese battery maker CATL.

Refining lower-grade nickel ores into battery materials requires large volumes of sulphuric acid for a process known as high-pressure acid leaching.

If supplies remain constrained, refiners could face higher production costs, delays and increased competition for feedstock, potentially flowing through to battery makers and EV...
body.zh: 中国已禁止出口硫酸，硫酸是世界上使用最广泛的工业化学品，也是电池和服装制造、化肥生产和金属加工业的关键成分。 今年早些时候，中东冲突扰乱了通过霍尔木兹海峡的硫磺运输，导致化学品供应面临压力。 悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究所的玛丽娜·张表示，虽然中国提出的禁令可能是暂时的，但它标志着澳大利亚最大贸易伙伴的政策转变，越来越优先考虑对工业投入的控制。 “这不仅仅是成品，还有上游材料、加工技术和基本工业原料，使先进制造业能够规模化……因此，虽然眼前的措施可能是暂时的，但潜在的逻辑是结构性的，”张告诉SBS新闻。 硫是用于生产硫酸的主要成分，这意味着海湾地区原材料的运输和加工延迟对依赖稳定供应的制造商产生了连锁效应。 到 2025 年，全球海运硫磺供应量的一半左右来自中东。 去年，中国占亚洲硫酸出口量的很大一部分，并且仍然是世界最大的出口国之一。这种供应的损失现在引起了已经在争相寻找替代来源的海外买家的担忧。 虽然预计影响将波及多个行业，但分析师表示，电池供应链可能是受影响最大的行业之一。 张说，这种情况“揭示了清洁能源转型核心的一个悖论……这取决于需要能源密集型、化学密集型且通常对环境困难的加工的矿物”。 “然而，许多西方国家花费了数十年的时间，将那些‘肮脏’的工业活动外包出去。” 硫酸在镍和铜等金属加工中也发挥着重要作用，这两种金属广泛用于电动汽车电池和储能系统。 印度尼西亚快速扩张的镍加工业被认为特别容易受到禁令的影响。 中国已成为全球电动汽车（EV）供应链中使用的电池级镍的主要生产国，其中包括与中国电池制造商宁德时代相关的制造商。 将低品位镍矿石精炼成电池材料需要大量硫酸，这一过程被称为高压酸浸出。 如果供应仍然受到限制，炼油厂可能面临更高的生产成本、延误和原料竞争加剧，并可能流向电池制造商和电动汽车……

reflection.en: The halt in sulphuric acid exports highlights the interconnectedness of global supply chains and the importance of foresight. When nations or industries rely heavily on single sources, prudence is needed to anticipate potential disruptions and prepare for their impact.
reflection.zh: 硫酸出口的暂停凸显了全球供应链的相互关联性以及预见性的重要。当国家或行业严重依赖单一来源时，需要审慎地预见潜在的干扰并为其影响做好准备。

title.en: As Xi sets a new power dynamic, Trump leaves China with little to brag about
title.zh: 习近平确立新权力格局，特朗普对中国无甚可夸耀

summary.en: A recent summit between the leaders of China and the United States, while largely cordial, indicated a potential shift in the balance of power between the two nations.
summary.zh: 在中美两国领导人的一次大致友好的峰会期间，有迹象表明两国之间的权力平衡可能正在发生变化。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump hailed it as “the biggest summit ever.” In reality, his less than 48 lavish hours in China yielded few results.

Expectations for any real breakthroughs were always low. But what we saw at the high-stakes summit could still shape the US-China relationship for months and years to come.

China had been signalling for weeks that Taiwan would be its top priority at this summit.

The island’s status has always been a point of conflict between the US and Chinese governments; China claims it as a self-governing province that will eventually be brought under its control, while the US has long been its single largest supplier of the weapons needed to prevent that from happening.

But this week, Chinese President Xi Jinping took it one step further; saying explicitly that from now on, the most important factor in the US-China relationship would be how the US deals with Taiwan.

“The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations,” Xi told Trump, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry handout. “If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. If handled poorly, the two countries will collide or even clash, putting the entire US-China relationship in an extremely dangerous situation.”

When asked for his version of events later in the day, Trump opted to say nothing. His silence was seen as a win in Taiwan, where fears he might go off script and say something to inadvertently shift the US’ position on the island were high going into the summit.

“US policy on the issue of Taiwan is unchanged as of today and as of the meeting that we had here today,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said. “It was raised. They always raised it on their side. We always make clear our position and we move on to other topics.”

But China has made its position clear; the US’ ongoing support for Taiwan could jeopardise one of its most important trade relationships.

The US approved a US$15b ($2.09b) arms package for Taiwan in December last year; its largest ever. But with Trump still yet to give his final approval, its delivery had been stalled.

Whether or not those weapons finally reach Taiwan may be the first real test of whether Xi’s threat made an impact.

While the summit was largely cordial, there were moments that signalled the balance of power between the two leaders might be shifting.

Xi rolled out the red carpet and did a lot to make Trump feel respected; sending his Vice President to greet him at the airport, personally accompanying him on a tour of the Temple of Heaven, and allowing him to visit the highly secretive Zhongnanhai compound, where he and other senior Chinese Communist...
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普称赞这是“有史以来规模最大的峰会”。事实上，他在中国度过的不到48个小时的奢华时光并没有取得什么成果。 对任何真正突破的期望总是很低。但我们在这次高风险峰会上看到的情况仍可能影响未来数月乃至数年的美中关系。 几周来，中国一直在暗示台湾将是此次峰会的首要任务。 该岛的地位一直是美国和中国政府之间的冲突点。中国声称它是一个自治省，最终将受到其控制，而美国长期以来一直是其最大的武器供应商，以防止这种情况发生。 但本周，中国国家主席习近平更进一步；明确表示，今后美中关系最重要的因素将是美国如何对待台湾。 根据中国外交部的讲义，习近平对特朗普说：“台湾问题是中美关系中最重要的问题。” “如果处理得当，双边关系将保持总体稳定。如果处理不好，两国就会发生冲突甚至冲突，使整个美中关系处于极其危险的境地。” 当天晚些时候，当被问及他对事件的看法时，特朗普选择什么也不说。他的沉默在台湾被视为一种胜利，在峰会上，人们非常担心他可能会脱离剧本，说出一些无意中改变美国在台湾的立场的话。 美国国务卿卢比奥表示：“截至今天以及我们今天在这里举行的会议，美国在台湾问题上的政策没有变化。” “有人提出了。他们总是站在自己一边提出。我们总是明确我们的立场，然后转向其他话题。” 但中方已经明确表明立场，美国对台湾的持续支持可能会危及其最重要的贸易关系之一。 去年 12 月，美国批准了一项价值 150 亿美元（2.09b 美元）的台湾军售计划；其规模有史以来最大。但由于特朗普尚未给予最终批准，其交付已陷入停滞。 这些武器最终是否到达台湾可能是习近平的威胁是否产生影响的第一个真正考验。 尽管这次峰会基本上是友好的，但有些时刻表明两位领导人之间的权力平衡可能正在发生变化。 习近平铺上红地毯，做了很多让特朗普感到受到尊重的事情；派副总统到机场迎接他，亲自陪同他游览天坛，并允许他参观高度保密的中南海大院，他和其他中共高级官员都在那里……

reflection.en: News of shifting power dynamics between nations reminds us that human authority is ultimately transient. Psalm 75:7 offers a profound perspective, reminding us that it is God who judges, lifting up one and bringing down another. This truth invites us to look beyond temporary political tides and trust in a higher, unchanging sovereignty.
reflection.zh: 国家间权力动态的变化提醒我们，人类的权威终究是暂时的。诗篇75:7提供了一个深刻的视角，提醒我们是雅伟施行审判，他使这人降卑，使那人升高。这一真理邀请我们超越暂时的政治潮流，信靠那至高无上、永不改变的主权。

title.en: Two dead from mosquito-borne virus as NT authorities urge precautions
title.zh: 北领地当局敦促采取预防措施，造成两人死于蚊媒病毒

summary.en: NT Health has recommended people take preventative measures, including using insect repellent and covering up.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two deaths from a mosquito-borne virus in an outback town have prompted a warning for people to cover up and use insect repellent.

Northern Territory health authorities on Tuesday confirmed two people had died from Murray Valley encephalitis (MVE).

The deaths occurred in Alice Springs in April and May, respectively, an NT Health spokesperson said.

A person can be infected with the rare and potentially fatal virus after a bite from an infected mosquito.

Transmission of the virus in the NT is most frequent between February and June, with most cases occurring between March and May.

Health authorities undertake mosquito surveillance and testing across the Top End for the virus from January to June each year.

Mosquito collecting and testing sites are currently operating in central Australia.

Symptoms of the virus include severe headache, fever, nausea and vomiting, muscle aches, drowsiness, confusion and seizures.

Water sources, including isolated pools, provide ideal breeding conditions for mosquitoes, which are most active after sundown, at night and early in the morning.

NT Health has encouraged residents and visitors to protect themselves by applying insect repellent containing DEET, picaridin or oil of lemon eucalyptus, to wear light-coloured protective clothing and to cover their feet.

They should also ensure tents are mosquito-proof, avoid mosquito-prone areas, especially after sundown, and use mosquito coils or mosquito lanterns for outdoor areas.

During a 2023 outbreak, eight cases were recorded, including two deaths and two cases resulting in severe neurological impairment.

For the latest from SBS News,  download our app and  subscribe to our newsletter .
body.zh: 内陆城镇有两人死于蚊媒病毒，这促使人们发出警告，要求人们遮盖衣服并使用驱虫剂。 北领地卫生当局周二证实，有两人死于墨累谷脑炎（MVE）。 北领地卫生局发言人表示，死亡事件分别发生在四月和五月。 被受感染的蚊子叮咬后，一个人可能会感染这种罕见且可能致命的病毒。 病毒在北领地的传播在二月至六月期间最频繁，大多数病例发生在三月至五月之间。 每年一月至六月，卫生当局都会在北端地区进行蚊子监测和病毒检测。 目前，澳大利亚中部正在运营蚊子收集和测试站。 该病毒的症状包括严重头痛、发烧、恶心和呕吐、肌肉酸痛、嗜睡、精神错乱和癫痫发作。 包括隔离水池在内的水源为蚊子提供了理想的繁殖条件，蚊子在日落后、夜间和清晨最为活跃。 北领地卫生局鼓励居民和游客使用含有避蚊胺、派卡瑞丁或柠檬桉油的驱虫剂来保护自己，穿浅色防护服并遮住脚部。 他们还应确保帐篷防蚊，避开蚊子多发区域，尤其是日落后，并在室外区域使用蚊香或蚊灯。 2023 年爆发期间，记录了 8 例病例，其中 2 例死亡，2 例导致严重神经损伤。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

title.en: 'Doesn't return by chance': Australia's 'deeply concerning' diphtheria outbreak, explained
title.zh: “并非偶然卷土重来”：澳大利亚“令人深感担忧”的白喉疫情解释道

summary.en: The vaccine that prevents this "ancient" disease is freely available. Experts say its resurgence is alarming.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Experts are warning Australia's diphtheria outbreak — which has spread across state borders from a cluster in the Northern Territory to Western Australia, Queensland and South Australia — exposes serious cracks in the country's public health system

Diphtheria was first described in ancient Greece and formally named in the 1800s.

In the 1930s, diphtheria was among the top-ten causes of child death, causing more than 4,000 deaths in Australia between 1926 and 1935.

Cases fell significantly following the introduction of vaccines in the 1940s. The disease is now considered rare in Australia.

NT Health is awaiting results from an autopsy report on a possible diphtheria-related death in the Northern Territory. If confirmed, it would be the first fatal case of the infectious disease in Australia since 2018.

Federal Health Minister Mark Butler told ABC Radio National on Tuesday he was "very concerned" about the outbreak and said it was Australia's worst in decades.

He said he had met with Aboriginal medical services in Alice Springs, where "almost all of the cases" were affecting Indigenous Australians. Staff there are "deeply concerned", Butler said.

"We're working with the NT government and the Aboriginal-controlled sector to get more vaccines there," he said.

Diphtheria is a potentially deadly infection caused by by certain strains of Corynebacterium bacteria.

The highly contagious microorganisms infect the skin and upper respiratory tract, and can produce diphtheria toxin.

Respiratory diphtheria causes severe, painful swelling of the throat and neck that can block the passage of air and cause breathing problems.

In cutaneous or skin infection cases, the bacteria can cause ulcers and local swelling.

Respiratory diphtheria is the more severe of the two presentations, and is potentially fatal, especially when it infects infants. No respiratory cases were recorded in children in Australia between 1992 and 2022.

Associate professor Erin Price, a microbiology researcher at the University of the Sunshine Coast, said early symptoms include a mild fever, sore throat, and swollen neck glands for respiratory diphtheria, or skin sores with local swelling and tissue damage in cutaneous cases.

"Symptoms can worsen as the bacterium blocks the airways, and the toxin can spread via blood, causing heart failure and paralysis," Price said.

Diphtheria bacteria can live in the nose, mouth or on infected skin lesions, and is spread through respiratory droplets, for example, from coughing or sneezing, or by touching infected lesions.

Professor Adrian Esterman is a Professor of Biostatistics and Epidemiology in the School of Public Health at Adelaide University.

title.en: Families 'terrified', have 'grave concerns' for Australians on Gaza flotilla detained by Israel
title.zh: 家庭“害怕”，对澳大利亚人对以色列拘留的加沙船队表示“严重担忧”

summary.en: The wellbeing of 11 Australian activists is unknown after their Gaza-bound flotilla was intercepted overnight.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Australian government is urgently seeking information on the whereabouts and condition of seven Australian activists allegedly detained by Israel after boats in a Gaza-bound aid flotilla were intercepted by the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) in international waters overnight.

The location and condition of the Australians remains unknown, and the flotilla's media delegate confirmed there had been no contact with the activists since the delegation was intercepted.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) said it was urgently seeking confirmation of the welfare of Australians it believed to be detained.

"We will continue to make clear our expectation that any detainees receive humane treatment in line with international norms," a DFAT spokesperson said on Tuesday.

Flotilla organisers identified the Australian activists as Anny Mokotow, Dr Bianca Webb-Pullman, Neve O'Connor, Violet Coco, Gemma O'Toole, Sam Woripa Watson, Zack Schofield, Helen O'Sullivan, Juliet Lamont, Isla Lamont and Surya McEwan.

The Israeli foreign ministry said on X, that activists from the "provocation flotilla" had been transferred to Israeli vessels and claimed that no aid had been found on their boats.

The missing Australians' parents and loved ones called for immediate government action at a conference at the State Library Victoria on Tuesday.

Julie Webb-Pullman, the mother of general practitioner Dr Bianca Webb-Pullman, said she hadn't heard from her daughter since 8.09pm on Monday, as the flotilla was intercepted.

"Serial kidnappers have done it again, abducted my daughter in international waters while she was delivering humanitarian aid," she told reporters.

"Yet our pathetic prime minister cannot even rustle up a condemnation, let alone demand accountability."

Susie O'Toole said she hadn't had any direct contact with her 23-year-old daughter, Gemma, and assumed the cohort was on a prison cargo ship bound for Ashdod prison in Israel.

"Most probably they've been left out in the sun like most people previously have been, held in stress positions, not given water, not given food," she said.

"We are terrified about Gemma's well-being, we demand the Australian government do everything they can to get her home safely."

Neve O'Connor's father said: "It was made clear to the Sumud participants that the IDF could not guarantee the safety of any of the prisoners on the prison ship, and that those that had been kidnapped the first time would get special treatment."

"Neve was one of those people, so we have grave concerns for Neve, and all the Global participants."

Advocates of trans rights are alarmed over pledges from the Opposition and conservative parties to tighten sex discrimination laws, saying such a move could remove key legal protections for the minority group.

Last week, the Federal Court upheld a 2024 decision that it was discriminatory to exclude a transgender user from a women-only app.

The court had been considering an appeal from Giggle for Girls app founder Sall Grover over the 2024 finding that she discriminated against Roxanne Tickle by blocking her from using the app and refusing to reinstate her.

Grover and Giggle argued the decision to exclude Tickle was exempt from being classed as discrimination because the app aimed to achieve "substantial equality" and create a safe space for women.

On Friday, the Federal Court upheld its decision that the exemption did not apply, meaning similar arguments made in defence of single-sex spaces would likely also fail.

On Saturday, Opposition leader Angus Taylor said in a statement on social media that the finding confirmed "the Australian law does not properly protect single sex spaces for women and girls".

He vowed on social media to amend the Sex Discrimination Act if the Coalition won government, "to ensure that women and girls (and men and boys) have protections based on biological sex".

"But we are recognising something that should never have been in doubt: biological sex is real, it matters, and women and girls deserve spaces where it is respected."

Taylor said a move to "define biological sex in the Act" as "the sex you are born" would be a first-term priority.

The Liberals' junior Coalition partner, the Nationals, echoed the sentiment, and One Nation leader Pauline Hanson was also sharply critical of the decision and pledged to back Grover in parliament.

LGBTIQ+ Health Australia's CEO Nicky Bath told SBS News that the Sex Discrimination Act makes a difference in trans and gender diverse people's lives.

Bath said the current legislation plays a role in protecting vulnerable people from discrimination and promoting equality.

"Changes to legislation in response to a single case do not represent due process."

Provisions against discrimination based on gender identity were introduced to the Sex Discrimination Act in 2013 by the Gillard government.

In March, the Australian Human Rights Commission found that trans and gender diverse people are discriminated against in education, healthcare, workplaces, housing, and the justice system.

More than 30 per cent of trans and gender diverse people have faced job discrimination, while over 56 per cent have been discriminated against in healthcare.

"Trans and gender diverse people experience significant health and wellbeing disparities compared to the general population," Bath said.

body.en:
Opposition leader Angus Taylor has dismissed criticism from a Liberal senator who has "deep concerns" over the Coalition's migration policy and fears it "alienates" migrants.

Andrew McLachlan, a senator for South Australia, on Tuesday told ABC Radio National the framing of Taylor's plan to link immigration with the number of homes being built each year risked alienating diaspora communities across the country.

"I don’t think our rhetoric meets the needs of the broader community. I think our rhetoric used alienates migrant communities," McLachlan said.

But McLachlan agreed there was a legitimate conversation to be had about migration levels, to ensure new arrivals get the support they need.

"It's about the tone and our approach, because we cannot — you should not — approach migration as a negative," McLachlan said.

"Certainly it should be controlled, and we don't want to invite people here without giving them a society that can accommodate them both economically and culturally, but we cannot continue to blame migrants for the problems of our economy."

In his budget reply speech last week , Taylor promised to set Australia's net overseas migration level at the number of homes completed in the previous year.

He argued this would curb "mass migration" from "running ahead of the homes, roads, hospitals, schools and services Australia can provide".

McLachlan took issue with the term, saying it was unacceptable and "creates fear and anxiety in the community".

"That is not the Liberal way. We are a party of the centre-right that was founded on core foundations of care for the individual and wanting them to meet their aspirations, and that includes compassion and humility."

The Opposition leader has also said a Coalition government would generate billions of dollars by cutting welfare — including the National Disability Insurance Scheme, Jobseeker, Youth Allowance and the Family Tax benefit — to non-citizens. Taylor clarified last week that this would include tax-paying permanent residents .

McLachlan said he is concerned this policy suite would create "two types of members in the community".

"I have deep concerns, coming from a multicultural community, that we are going to create two types of members in the community going forward with this policy suite," McLachlan said.

"If you’re both contributing to the wealth of the nation and one is entitled to certain entitlements, you could have almost a form of a strata-ing of our society. And I'm not sure that’s the Australian way."

Asked about the senator's remarks, Taylor denied his comments alienated migrants.

title.en: Police charge man with triple murder after woman and children found dead in Sydney home
