summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A man has been charged with three counts of murder after police discovered the bodies of his wife and two children inside a home, in a "particularly violent" scene.

The bodies were found in south-west Sydney after a call to triple-zero from the home shortly before 8pm on Monday, police said.

Officers entered the home on Raymond Avenue in Campbelltown and found the bodies of two boys, aged four and 12, and a 46-year-old woman inside.

A 47-year-old man was arrested at the scene and taken to Campbelltown Police Station, where he was charged with three counts of murder and refused bail.

Acting superintendent Michael Moroney said police believe the three victims were the arrested man's wife and children.

Despite the horrific nature of the crime, police had no prior knowledge of domestic violence incidents at the home.

"Whilst I can't give you specific information in regards to how they passed, what I can tell you is that all three persons sustained significant injuries and it was a particularly violent crime scene," Moroney told ABC News on Tuesday.

"What this does is really highlight the scourge that domestic violence is across society."

The alleged murders follow a four-day police blitz on known domestic violence offenders by NSW Police that resulted in nearly 1,000 arrests.

Between Wednesday and Saturday, 993 people were arrested and 2,063 charges were laid, with 299 arrest warrants executed.

title.en: No gloves, no approval: Inside the fight club bringing bare knuckle boxing to backyards
title.zh: 没有手套，没有批准：在搏击俱乐部内将裸指关节拳击带到后院

summary.en: For these men, the desire to fight in bare knuckle backyard bouts outweighs the risk of injury or even imprisonment.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A jumping castle is inflated outside a red-brick house in Sydney. In the backyard, a barbecue fires meat for the men, women and children piling in for the event on Australia Day.

People stand around with drinks, laughing, mingling. For a moment, it could be a family get-together.

Then you notice the rubber mats and remember why everyone is here. They’ve come to watch men fight bare knuckle. Some fighters have driven interstate for a single three-minute round.

The address is spread around just before the event. It is invite-only and not approved by the NSW Combat Sports Authority.

In a statement to The Feed, the NSW Combat Sports Authority said anyone who arranges, holds or takes part in a combat sport contest outside the Combat Sports Act may be committing a criminal offence, with serious penalties , including imprisonment.

Under NSW combat sport rules, gloves must be worn in boxing. The authority said it considered last year whether bare knuckle contests should be exempted, but determined they would not.

It’s why, organiser and former fighter Randall Rayment, 39, says they’ve had to congregate like this.

Known online as "The Limb Reaper", Randall is a retired MMA fighter, jiu-jitsu black belt and boxer. These days, he says bare knuckle is the fight style he cares about most.

"The rules are basically, you respect everyone," he tells The Feed. "If you're going to be a g ronk, you're kicked out, the fight’s stopped."

Though the group has gathered on Australia Day, he says they’re apolitical: "We just want to enjoy the day."

It is not a polished fight event. There is no prize money, no official winner and, at times, the weight classes appear loose.

"We couldn't really have scales and shit here," Randall says to the people about to fight. "We're going to try and weigh you up as close as we can."

There is no doctor, no referee, no judges, because he says the day is just "sparring" — not a contest.

Two opponents are stepping forward to aim fists at each other’s heads. And around the mats, the crowd cheers them on, people are coaching, filming the event and picking a side.

One of the fighters is Tui, who goes by "Tui Knuckles". The 20-year-old is trying to make a name for himself in the sport, and he’s driven nine hours from Queensland to Sydney for the event. He’s on the backyard "main card".

"I've been fighting pretty much most of my life, just only on the street because I grew up in Logan [an outer region of Brisbane]," he tells The Feed.

Above his right eye is a scar, about an inch long. Tui says it came from a Stanley knife attack when he was 14.

For him, fighting was not just sport. It was survival — something he did so he would not get "walked over".

title.en: Why this migrant newspaper is still thriving — a century later
title.zh: 澳大利亚历史最悠久的移民报纸之一如何仍在制造头条新闻

summary.en: For a century, The Greek Herald newspaper has served Greek Australians, maintaining their connection to language, community, and culture across generations.
summary.zh: 一百年来，《希腊先驱报》这份报纸一直服务于澳大利亚的希腊裔社区，帮助几代希腊裔澳大利亚人维系着他们的语言、社群和文化。

body.en:
The presses have rolled, the stories have travelled, and for 100 years, Australia's Greek community has kept turning the pages of their treasured community newspaper.

"You gotta have a newspaper, you can't depend on TV all the time," says George Thanos, who remembers reading the Greek Herald as a child in the 1950s when he and his family arrived in Australia.

"We used to go to the Greek church on Saturday or Sunday, and they give you a paper," he says.

"The Greek Herald helped a lot. We could read what was going on in Australia, what's going on overseas. We all used to depend on the paper to get along, advertise for jobs, and it was a very good communication system."

For many Greek and Cypriot post-war arrivals, the paper was a lifeline for those who were still learning to speak English.

"The time when we came here, we didn't speak much English. Only 'yes' and 'no'," Charalambos Kokotsis recalls.

"The Greek newspaper... it was one thing we read. It was something good for us."

Decades later the community still depends on the paper, Kokotsis says, to catch up on "funerals, memorials, sports and a little bit of news".

And it remains a ritual for many in Australia's Greek kafenios — coffee houses — and community clubs.

Now in his 90s, Pantelis Christou still travels to Sydney's Cyprus Club every other day.

The Greek Herald began in 1926 as a modest broadsheet called The Hellenic Herald, and has since grown into a national institution.

While documenting abandoned Greek villages in the 1980s, historical researchers Leonard Janiszewski and Effy Alexakis discovered copies of the newspaper had been sent back to Greece.

For relatives back home, the paper was a powerful symbol of possibility, Janiszewski says, showing that a Greek community could thrive on the other side of the world.

"What it was telling them was not just simply that there was a community here, but there was a community in which you had churches, a community where you could go to a Greek barber, you could go to a Greek shop, you could go to a Greek store," he tells SBS News.

In 1971, the paper was bought by publisher Theo Skalkos, a larger-than-life media figure once described as the "Greek Murdoch".

In a 1996 SBS interview, Skalkos joked that he and Murdoch were "like brothers".

Under his leadership, the publication expanded dramatically, becoming the only daily Greek-language newspaper published outside Greece and Cyprus.

Printing presses have rolled every single day from 1972 onward, an extraordinary feat for an ethnic community newspaper in Australia.

Skalkos also owned several other mastheads in different languages, driving an ethnic community media empire in Australia.

body.zh: 媒体不断滚动，故事不断传播，一百年来，澳大利亚的希腊社区不断翻阅他们珍贵的社区报纸。 “你必须有一份报纸，你不能一直依赖电视，”乔治·萨诺斯 (George Thanos) 说道，他记得小时候在 20 世纪 50 年代和家人抵达澳大利亚时读过《希腊先驱报》。 “我们过去常常在周六或周日去希腊教堂，他们会给你一张纸，”他说。 “希腊先驱报帮了很大的忙。我们可以了解澳大利亚正在发生的事情，海外正在发生的事情。我们过去都依靠报纸来相处，发布招聘广告，这是一个非常好的沟通系统。” 对于许多战后抵达的希腊和塞浦路斯人来说，这份报纸是那些仍在学习说英语的人的生命线。 “当我们来到这里的时候，我们不太会说英语。只会说‘是’和‘不是’，”查拉兰博斯·科科齐斯回忆道。 “希腊报纸……这是我们读的一件事。这对我们有好处。” 科科齐斯说，几十年后，社区仍然依靠报纸来了解“葬礼、追悼会、体育运动和一些新闻”。 对于澳大利亚希腊 kafenios（咖啡馆）和社区俱乐部中的许多人来说，这仍然是一种仪式。 现在已经 90 多岁的潘泰利斯·克里斯图 (Pantelis Christou) 仍然每隔一天前往悉尼的塞浦路斯俱乐部 (Cyprus Club)。 《希腊先驱报》始建于 1926 年，最初是一份名为《希腊先驱报》的普通大报，现已发展成为一家全国性机构。 在记录 20 世纪 80 年代废弃的希腊村庄时，历史研究人员 Leonard Janiszewski 和 Effy Alexakis 发现报纸的副本已被送回希腊。 雅尼谢夫斯基说，对于家乡的亲戚来说，这张报纸是可能性的有力象征，表明希腊社区可以在世界的另一边蓬勃发展。 “它告诉他们的不仅仅是这里有一个社区，还有一个有教堂的社区，一个你可以去希腊理发店、你可以去希腊商店、你可以去希腊商店的社区，”他告诉 SBS 新闻。 1971 年，该报被出版商 Theo Skalkos 收购，后者是一位传奇的媒体人物，曾被称为“希腊默多克”。 1996年，斯卡尔科斯在接受SBS采访时开玩笑说，他和默多克“就像兄弟一样”。 在他的领导下，该出版物急剧扩张，成为希腊和塞浦路斯以外出版的唯一一份希腊语日报。 从 1972 年起，印刷机每天都在滚动，这对于澳大利亚少数民族社区报纸来说是一项非凡的壮举。 斯卡尔科斯还拥有其他几个不同语言的报头，推动着澳大利亚的少数民族社区媒体帝国。 在他执掌公司 40 年后，他的女儿 Dimitra Skalkos 接替了他的职位。

reflection.en: This story highlights the enduring human desire to preserve heritage and pass it on to future generations. Like the psalmist's call to tell of past wonders, a newspaper like The Greek Herald plays a vital role in ensuring that language, community, and culture continue to thrive and connect people across time.
reflection.zh: 这个故事突显了人类传承遗产、将其传递给后代的持久愿望。正如诗篇作者呼吁向后代讲述雅伟的奇妙作为，像《希腊先驱报》这样的报纸在确保语言、社群和文化持续繁荣并跨越时间连接人们方面，扮演着至关重要的角色。

title.en: Ex-Qantas boss seeks to launch new budget Australian airline
title.zh: 澳洲航空前老板寻求创办新的澳大利亚廉价航空公司

summary.en: An aviation industry expert said an ultra-low-budget airline could bring ticket prices down across the board.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A proposed new budget airline could bring ticket prices down across Australia's busiest aviation routes, but experts warn it would face immense challenges from existing players.

Former Qantas executive Peter Kelly is backing new airline, Zinc, as a cheaper alternative for Australians.

Modelled on European low-cost carrier Ryanair, Zinc is promising the cheapest domestic tickets — initially between the "Golden Triangle" of Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane, then Adelaide and the Gold Coast.

Unfazed by challenges, Kelly is firm that the new Western Sydney International Airport will enable enough flights for Zinc to be viable.

The Australian domestic market was previously impeded by a limited number of "slots" available for flights through Sydney's existing Kingsford Smith Airport.

Professor Rico Merkert, an aviation industry expert from the University of Sydney, said an ultra-low budget airline like Zinc has the potential to bring ticket prices down across the board.

"For customers, it would be great. More competition means lower prices," Merkert said.

He said Jetstar, the low-budget subsidiary of Kelly's former employer, will fight to maintain its most profitable routes.

Defunct airline Rex expanded its regional roots to offer flights in the "Golden Triangle" — a decision that led to its collapse, Merkert said.

Kelly believes that there's an appetite for more competition in Australia, not least by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.

Considering the global fuel crisis and the recent failure of American low-cost airline Spirit, Merkert said it's "crazy" to launch an airline.

"It's an absolute crazy environment to set up an airline right now, when most other airlines are just trying to understand how they can survive," he said.

RMIT aviation expert Chrystal Zhang agrees that timing is critical for new airlines. However, she believes pre-launch preparation could see better outcomes for the airline's future.

"New airlines entering the market would face significant and very head-on competition from the incumbent airlines," she said.

"In theory, we need more airlines, but in reality, perhaps it's a different story."

body.zh: 拟议的新廉价航空公司可能会降低澳大利亚最繁忙的航线的票价，但专家警告称，它将面临现有航空公司的巨大挑战。 澳洲航空前高管彼得·凯利（Peter Kelly）支持新航空公司 Zinc，作为澳大利亚人更便宜的选择。 Zinc 效仿欧洲廉价航空公司瑞安航空，承诺提供最便宜的国内机票——首先是悉尼、墨尔本和布里斯班“金三角”之间的航班，然后是阿德莱德和黄金海岸之间的航班。 凯利没有被挑战所困扰，他坚信新的西悉尼国际机场将为 Zinc 提供足够的航班。 此前，澳大利亚国内市场因经过悉尼现有金斯福德·史密斯机场的航班“起降时刻”数量有限而受到阻碍。 悉尼大学航空业专家 Rico Merkert 教授表示，像 Zinc 这样的超低成本航空公司有可能全面降低机票价格。 “对于客户来说，这会很棒。更多的竞争意味着更低的价格，”默克特说。 他表示，凯利前雇主的低成本子公司捷星航空将努力维持其最赚钱的航线。 默克特表示，已停业的雷克斯航空公司扩大了其地区业务，在“金三角”提供航班，这一决定导致了该公司的倒闭。 凯利认为，澳大利亚希望加强竞争，尤其是澳大利亚竞争和消费者委员会的竞争。 考虑到全球燃油危机和美国廉价航空公司精神航空最近的失败，默克特表示，创办一家航空公司是“疯狂的”。 他说：“现在建立一家航空公司绝对是一个疯狂的环境，而大多数其他航空公司只是想了解如何才能生存。” 皇家墨尔本理工大学航空专家 Chrystal 张 同意，时机对于新航空公司来说至关重要。然而，她相信启动前的准备工作可以为航空公司的未来带来更好的成果。 “进入市场的新航空公司将面临来自现有航空公司的激烈且非常正面的竞争，”她说。 “理论上，我们需要更多的航空公司，但实际上，情况可能有所不同。” 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。
